claim: Adjuncts placed to the left of their expected position, as in [14iib] The party will long be remembered, “are found with a very restricted range of adjuncts: compare, for example, The supply will be drastically reduced with ∗The supply will drastically be reduced.”
evidence_summary: CGEL’s own prose puts a range of ·ly adverbs before passive be: some can readily be used (p. 366), bare NPs can optionally be used (p. 410), can usefully be subdivided (p. 425), would traditionally be treated (p. 600), has subsequently been changed (p. 701). Ch. 6’s ?-marked manner adjuncts before an auxiliary (pp. 575, 578) point the same way.
finding: Unresolved. These examples count against the claim only if the adverb belongs semantically with the participle, which is the reader’s analysis, not CGEL’s, and most have a reading with scope over the be clause. Readily and optionally are the likeliest cases, and a corpus search for manner adverbs in this slot (will carefully be + past participle) would decide.
inference: Is leftward incongruent placement limited to a very restricted range of adjuncts?

evidence.passage: §20.2, p. 784. “found with a very restricted range of adjuncts”
evidence.example: Page 366, some can readily be used. Page 410, bare NPs can optionally be used.
evidence.establishes: A lead only. The book’s own usage is evidence against the claim only on the incongruent reading.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
